title: Rational Hearing
idiom: hand-coloured 15th-century music-theory woodcut, two strings in two and three loops, the sounding one red
hero_prompt: Hand-coloured woodcut in the manner of a 15th-century Italian music-theory book, black ink on cream with a single accent of engineering red, hand-made on paper, flat and graphic with visible woodcut line and watercolour texture, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field, wide panoramic composition: across the foreground, large and close, a long plain wooden box with two strings stretched along its top, both inked red and drawn as vibrating standing waves; each string is doubled into an upper curve and a mirrored lower curve that meet in points, so the upper string makes two long pointed closed loops touching end to end, and the lower string makes three long pointed closed loops touching end to end. Behind, smaller, a row of plain unmarked bronze bells in falling sizes hangs from a wooden beam, and two open organ pipes stand, one longer than the other. An old woman scholar in a long robe stands at the far end with her back to us, head tilted, listening. Cream, black, ochre and one red.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on a warm cream ground, no shading or gradients: two thick strings stretched side by side between two solid posts, the upper string swelling into two loops and the lower into three loops. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
